lessons.title: What's the Weather Like?
lessons.changes: Shortened and simplified for independent kindergarten reading; kept Annie's letter frame; removed the map, polar and rainforest sections; comprehension questions rewritten as choices with text evidence.

passage.title: What's the Weather Like?
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, Hello! My name is Annie. I live in a big city called Washington, D.C. I will be your weather pen pal. There are many kinds of weather. It can be sunny, cloudy, windy, rainy, or stormy. The weather changes day by day. There are four seasons in a year: winter, spring, summer, and autumn. Winter is the coldest season. In spring, new plants grow and flowers bloom. Summer is the hottest season. In autumn, the leaves fall from the trees. Autumn is also called fall. The seasons always change in the same order, year after year. This is called a cycle. Your friend, Annie

lessons.title: Winter
lessons.changes: Shortened and simplified; kept the thermometer, winter clothing, snow and Chinese New Year (red paper, red envelopes); removed other holidays, snow shoveling and snowplow sections; questions rewritten with text evidence; writing task added.

passage.title: Winter
passage.text: Dear Kindergartners, Today I will tell you about winter. Winter is the coldest season of the year. Winter includes December, January, and February. A thermometer tells us how hot or cold it is. When it is cold, the liquid in the thermometer stays down low. In winter, people wear hats, mittens, and scarves to stay warm. When it is very cold, rain can turn into snow. I love to build snowmen and go sledding! Winter has fun holidays, too. At Chinese New Year, homes are decorated with red paper. Children get red envelopes for good luck. What do you like best about winter? Your friend, Annie

lessons.title: The Grasshopper and the Ants
lessons.from: Lesson 6: The Grasshopper and the Ants
lessons.changes: Shortened the fable; dialogue rewritten as "X said, ..." so each sentence stands alone; removed the summer song and the ants' unkind reply, kept the closing song; questions rewritten, the lesson-of-the-story question tagged as a grade 1 stretch (RL.1.2).

tasks.title: Read: The Grasshopper and the Ants

passage.title: The Grasshopper and the Ants
passage.text: On a fine summer day, a grasshopper hopped in a field. He sang and danced all day long. Nearby, the ants worked hard. They filled their house with food for the long, cold winter. The grasshopper said, “Come and play with me!” But the ants kept working. Then autumn came, and the leaves fell from the trees. Soon it was winter. The grasshopper was cold and hungry. He knocked on the ants' door and asked, “May I share your food?” The ants asked, “What did you do all summer?” The grasshopper said, “I sang and danced in the sun.” As he walked away, he sang, “Next time I'll work as well as dance. Then I'll be ready, like the ants!”
